question.text: A machine gun fires a bullet of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>40</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> with a velocity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1200</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The man holding it can exert a maximum force of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>144</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></math> on the gun. The maximum number of bullets that the man can fire per second is

solution.text:
Suppose he can fire n bullets per second

∴  Force = Change in momentum per second

144=n⁡×(401000)×(1200)

n⁡=144×100040×1200 

n⁡=3
